What a good portfolio website actually needs
Before you open any tool, it helps to know what a portfolio site is actually for: giving someone 30 seconds to decide you're worth a longer look. That means a handful of things matter far more than clever design tricks.
Work samples or case studies.
Not just a logo grid � a few pieces with enough context that a stranger understands what you did and why it mattered.
An about section.
Who you are, what you do, and what you're looking for. Two or three paragraphs is plenty.
A way to get in touch.
Email, a contact form, or both. Make it impossible to miss.
A link to your resume or CV.
Recruiters and clients both look for this first, especially on mobile.
Get those four right and the rest � color palette, fonts, layout � is polish. Get them wrong and no amount of polish saves the site.
The one-prompt approach
The fastest way to build a portfolio site with Kodely is to describe the whole thing in one message: who you are, what you do, the sections you want, and the tone you're going for. Kodely reads that description and generates a complete site around it � structure, copy placeholders, and layout � in one pass, then shows you a live preview of the actual app as it's built.
You don't need to plan every section in advance. A rough, specific description beats a vague, exhaustive one. Name your field, mention two or three real projects, and say what you want visitors to do when they land on the page.
